subject: Logic
title: Decidability
description: A micro-lesson that makes Decidability usable.

hook.text: Can a computer always determine whether a logical statement is true or false? Sometimes, no.

buildup.text: A system is decidable if there's an algorithm that can determine the truth of any statement in it.

discovery.text: Propositional logic is decidable—truth tables always work. Predicate logic is not always decidable.

twist.text: Alonzo Church and Alan Turing independently proved this in 1936. Some questions are algorithmically unsolvable.

climax.text: Undecidability isn't a bug—it's a fundamental limit of computation and formal reasoning.

quiz.question: What does it mean for a system to be decidable?
options: An algorithm can determine truth of any statement
